candidates.label: Right optic nerve glioblastoma (WHO grade IV) with intraocular extension and secondary combined central retinal artery and vein occlusion
Right optic nerve anaplastic astrocytoma (WHO grade III) with intraocular extension and secondary retinal vascular occlusion
Malignant optic nerve glioma (high-grade astrocytoma) with vitreous seeding and combined central retinal artery and vein occlusion
Primary central nervous system lymphoma involving right optic nerve and vitreous
Inflammatory optic neuritis with secondary retinal vascular occlusion

response.rationale: Vitreous biopsy showing astrocytic neoplasm with GFAP positivity and ATRX loss strongly indicates a glial tumor, favoring high-grade optic nerve glioma. The acute vision loss and combined CRAO/CRVO suggest intraocular extension causing vascular compromise. Absence of inflammatory cells and LP abnormalities argue against optic neuritis. Anaplastic astrocytoma (D2) is plausible but glioblastoma (D1) more likely given the rapid progression and severe presentation. Lymphoma and inflammatory etiologies are contradicted by biopsy findings.
